subtopics.title: What Is the Internet?
subtopics.summary: Introduces the Internet from a nuts-and-bolts view (end systems, communication links, packet switches, ISPs), a services view supporting distributed applications, and defines what a protocol is and why all Internet communication is governed by protocols.

subtopics.title: The Network Edge
subtopics.summary: Covers end systems (hosts) and how they connect to the network: access networks such as DSL, cable, FTTH, Ethernet, WiFi, and cellular, plus guided and unguided physical media (twisted pair, coax, fiber, radio).

subtopics.title: The Network Core
subtopics.summary: Examines the mesh of links and packet switches at the Internet's core: store-and-forward packet switching and statistical multiplexing, circuit switching with FDM/TDM, and the Internet's structure as a network of networks of ISPs.

subtopics.title: Delay, Loss, and Throughput
subtopics.summary: Builds quantitative models for packet-switched networks: processing, queuing, transmission, and propagation delays; queuing delay and packet loss; end-to-end delay; and throughput including the bottleneck-link model.

subtopics.title: Protocol Layers and Service Models
subtopics.summary: Explains why networks use a layered architecture, the service each layer provides, the five-layer Internet protocol stack, and how messages are encapsulated layer-by-layer as they traverse the sender's and receiver's stacks.

subtopics.title: Networks Under Attack
subtopics.summary: Surveys prevalent Internet security attacks, including malware (viruses and worms), denial-of-service attacks, packet sniffing, and IP spoofing, motivating the study of network security.

subtopics.title: History of Computer Networking
subtopics.summary: Traces the development of packet switching and the evolution of computer networking and the Internet from its early research origins to today's Internet.
